A region in the $xy$-plane is bounded by the curve $y=2{cos}^{2}⁡x+x-1,$ the $x$-axis and the lines $x=\frac{\pi }{2}$ and $x=\frac{3\pi }{2},$ as shown above. The area of the region is

$A=$
{{field-1}}
worked_solution:
The area of the region is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}A={\int }_{\pi /2}^{3\pi /2}(2{cos}^{2}⁡x+x-1)\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

To calculate this integral, we use the double-angle formula for cosine that involves the ${cos}^{2}⁡x$ term, given by

$$
\operatorname{cos}⁡2x=2{cos}^{2}⁡x-1.
$$

 

Rearranging, we have

$$
{cos}^{2}⁡x=\frac{1}{2}(\operatorname{cos}⁡2x+1).
$$

Substituting this into our integral, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}A & ={\int }_{\pi /2}^{3\pi /2}(2{cos}^{2}⁡x+x-1)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{\pi /2}^{3\pi /2}[(\operatorname{cos}⁡2x+1)+x-1]\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{\pi /2}^{3\pi /2}(\operatorname{cos}⁡2x+x)\text{d}x \\  & ={(\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡2x+\frac{1}{2}{x}^{2})|}_{\pi /2}^{3\pi /2} \\  & =[\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(3\pi )+\frac{1}{2}{(\frac{3\pi }{2})}^{2}]-[\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi )+\frac{1}{2}{(\frac{\pi }{2})}^{2}] \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(\frac{9{\pi }^{2}}{4}-\frac{{\pi }^{2}}{4}) \\  & ={\pi }^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
